v.title: PSG’s Winning Streak Stalls as Roma Deliver the Ultimate Test
v.excerpt: Luis Enrique praises Roma’s 2‑2 draw that halted PSG’s 12‑game winning streak, hinting at a shift in European power dynamics.
v.body:
## Quick take
Luis Enrique admitted that Roma was the toughest match of the season for PSG, after a hard‑fought 2‑2 draw ended the club’s 12‑game run of victories. The result means the Parisians will have to regroup before the next Champions League showdown.

## What happened
On Wednesday’s Champions League clash, PSG and Roma were locked in a tense battle that saw both sides create chances but struggled to convert. The game began with a quick goal from PSG’s Kylian Mbappé, but Roma responded with a stunning strike from Federico Chiesa, leveling the score. The match settled into a defensive stalemate, with both teams pulling the ball out of the penalty area and only one clear shot each.

In the second half, Roma’s defensive line, masterminded by new coach Luis Enrique, held firm. A late corner by PSG was denied by a last‑minute save from Roma’s goalkeeper, and the final whistle confirmed a 2‑2 draw. The result was a shock for the French side, who had been unbeaten in all competitions for almost a year.

## Why it matters
- **For Barcelona**: The draw signals that PSG’s dominance is not guaranteed. If Barça’s rivals can hold off Roma, it suggests a shift in power dynamics that could benefit our own title push, especially if we can maintain consistency against the top teams.
- **For Luis Enrique**: The coach’s praise for Roma’s resilience shows he has found a tactical edge that could be mirrored against Barcelona. His emphasis on defensive solidity might inspire Barca’s own defensive strategies in upcoming fixtures.
- **For the Champions League**: A draw against Roma removes a psychological hurdle for PSG, but it also opens the door for other teams to challenge their supremacy. The result indicates that the competition will become more unpredictable, raising the stakes for every match.

## What's next
Barcelona’s next match against Real Madrid is looming. With PSG’s winning streak halted, the pressure on La Liga rivals to perform is higher than ever. Watch how Barcelona’s defense adapts to the tactical lessons from Luis Enrique’s Roma side, especially in the way they counter high‑press attacks. The outcome could set the tone for the rest of the season and decide whether Barcelona can maintain its edge over the top clubs.

*Source: [Luis Enrique calls Roma PSG's toughest test of the season after winning streak ends](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/50599458/luis-enrique-praises-roma-draw-halts-psg-winning-streak)*
